subject: mathematics
question_text: If f(x) = (sin²x + cos⁴x)/(cos²x + sin⁴x), show that f(2016) = 1.

mark_split.label: Reduce both halves to one letter

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.14, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 22. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 shape gives one mark to reducing both halves to t² − t + 1 and one to the conclusion that f is the constant 1, because the number 2016 does no work in this question and no mark can rest on it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would show f(2016) = 1 — what you substitute, and why the number 2016 does not matter.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write both halves in one letter
steps.margin_note: First mark is both halves reduced to t² − t + 1. Show the expansion of (1 − t)² in full; that is where the sign slip happens.
steps.memory_tip: Everything is sin²x and cos²x, so name one of them t. Then sin²x = 1 − t and both halves become the same quadratic.
lines: Put t = cos²x, so sin²x = 1 − t.

recall.must_convey: That with t = cos²x both the numerator and the denominator become t² − t + 1.
accept: let t be cos squared x so sin squared x is one minus t
the numerator becomes one minus t plus t squared
the denominator becomes t plus one minus t whole squared which is the same quadratic
cos square x ni t ani pettukunte rendu halves same avuthai
both top and bottom come to t squared minus t plus one
reject: use sin squared plus cos squared equals one
heard_as: t squared minus t plus one

steps.why: Both halves are built only from sin²x and cos²x, and sin²x + cos²x = 1 ties them together. Writing everything in the single letter t = cos²x turns each half into a quadratic in t, and the two quadratics can then be compared directly. Putting x = 2016 into the original fraction leads nowhere, because sin 2016 and cos 2016 have no exact value.
common_mistakes: Reading cos⁴x as cos 4x rather than (cos²x)².
Putting x = 2016 into the fraction first; the expression has to be simplified before any number is used.

steps.label: f is the constant 1
steps.margin_note: Second mark is the statement that f(x) = 1 for every real x, and only then f(2016) = 1. Say the denominator is never zero. Check with x = 1 radian: top and bottom both come to 0.7933.
steps.memory_tip: The top and the bottom are the same expression, so f is the constant 1. The number 2016 changes nothing.
lines: The two halves are the same expression.
so the denominator is never zero and f(x)
is defined for every x ∈ R.
∴ f(x) = 1 for every real x, and 2016 is

recall.must_convey: That the numerator equals the denominator, so f(x) = 1 for every real x, and 2016 is only one such value.
accept: top and bottom are equal so f of x is one for every real x
the function is the constant one so any input gives one
the denominator is never zero so f is defined everywhere and equals one
top bottom same kabatti f of x always one
two thousand sixteen is nothing special the answer is one for any number
reject: hence f of two thousand sixteen is one
then I substitute two thousand sixteen

steps.why: Because the two halves reduce to the same expression, f(x) = 1 for every real x. So f(2016) is not a special evaluation at all — the simplification is the answer, and 2016 could be replaced by any number. The denominator t² − t + 1 = (t − 1/2)² + 3/4 is at least 3/4, so it is never zero and f is defined on the whole of R.
common_mistakes: Writing f(2016) = 1 with no simplification above it; the marks are for the simplification.
Treating 2016 as degrees and reducing it by 360; x is a real number and the value is 1 either way.
Leaving out the check that the denominator is never zero.
